title: Foundry/OSAT due-diligence rule in practice (2025-2026): approved and authorised IC designers, KYC and reporting, and effect on Chinese fabless access to advanced foundry capacity
why_it_matters: Since January 2025 US rules make foundries and packaging houses screen every advanced logic chip for hidden AI accelerators. This shifts compliance cost onto foundries and may shut Chinese designers out of leading-edge capacity; the deadlines keep moving (now 31 Dec 2026).
questions: Which companies are on the approved IC designer (Supp. 6) and approved OSAT (Supp. 7) lists, and how have the lists changed?
What do foundries (TSMC, Samsung, UMC, GlobalFoundries) disclose about compliance costs and lost China revenue from the rule?
How many Chinese fabless companies relied on 16/14 nm-or-below foreign foundry capacity before 2025?
primary_sources: 90 FR 5298 and supplements 6-7 to 15 CFR Part 744
TSMC 20-F and annual report risk factors

title: US Section 232 action on polysilicon (Proclamation 11052, August 2026) and BIS anti-stockpiling rule: scope, duties and effects on wafer supply
why_it_matters: A new 2026 US import measure covers polysilicon, the raw material for all silicon wafers, with import adjustments from 4 December 2026; its effect on semiconductor-grade wafer supply versus solar is unclear.
questions: What does Proclamation 11052 impose (tariff levels, covered HS codes, exclusions for semiconductor-grade polysilicon)?
How does the BIS anti-stockpiling rule (91 FR 60505) work and whom does it hit?
Which US and foreign wafer/polysilicon suppliers are exposed?
